newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS STABLE WEEK EASIER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS STABLE WEEK EASIER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar, stable for most of the week, closed Friday mixed against the hard currencies but dealers forecast continued stability next week on the back of stronger tobacco-related foreign currency inflows.
The local dollar closed Friday at 11.3025/3125 against the key U.S. currency, unchanged from its opening level but some two cents down compared to its Monday level of around 11.3215.
Dealers reported some large payments that were generally matched by inflows composed of tobacco and mineral export receipts, leaving the Reserve bank inactive.
"We should see more tobacco money coming in next week and more central bank activity," one dealer told Reuters.
"This week the market struck a balance and there has been a natural mop-up of excess funds," he said, adding:"We still expect a stable dollar but inflation is complicating things."
Analysts expect annual inflation, measured at 19.9 percent in the year to March, to rise further in April on the back of a spate of price increases.

Against the pound, the Zimbabwe dollar closed firmer at 18.2739/3014 after opening at 18.3729/4027. It however lost against the rand at 2.5325/5364 compared to 2.5316/5356 and against the mark to 6.6811/6900 after opening at 6.6297/6395.
